description: Welsh register audit list. 'formal' = literary Welsh (Cymraeg Llenyddol) form dead in speech; 'preferred' = Cymraeg Byw colloquial form the deck targets. Deck defaults: ti casual / chi formal-plural. Severity: 'high' = dead in speech, swap wherever it appears in conversational cards; 'medium' = written-leaning, swap in beginner content. See docs/welsh-register-policy.md.

literary_forms.rationale: Literary-Welsh verb morphology and particles that no speaker uses in conversation; the colloquial forms are what Dysgu Cymraeg courses teach.

entries.note: Literary first-person copula; speech is dw i (or rydw i in careful/taught register).

entries.rom: nid wyf → dw i ddim (I am not)
entries.note: Literary negation; colloquial Welsh negates with ddim.
The preverbal particle y(r) is literary; speech drops it.

entries.preferred: gen i / gynnon ni (N) or gyda fi / gyda ni (S)
entries.rom: gennyf → gen i / gyda fi (with me, I have)
entries.note: Literary inflected preposition. Keep North or South forms consistent within a card.

entries.preferred: cael passive (mae'n cael ei weld, cafodd ei wneud)
entries.rom: gwelir → mae'n cael ei weld (is seen)
entries.note: Impersonal forms are written/official Welsh. Signage («ni chaniateir ysmygu») is genre language — exempt when quoted.
Speech always contracts; the full form reads literary. sydd sentence-finally («pwy sydd?» → «pwy sy?») follows the same pattern.
